newsitem.title: USA: CSCE to investigate coffee stock reporting errors.
newsitem.headline: CSCE to investigate coffee stock reporting errors.

text.p: The Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange said Thursday it plans to investigate errors in reporting stocks made by one of its warehouses, but maintained there was no evidence of market manipulation.
"The exchange will conduct an investigation involving its Warehouse and Licensing Committee," a CSCE spokeswoman said. "It was a warehouse error, there are no other forces at play."

CSCE said the certified stock total of 5,583 bags reported Monday was correct, but that the surprisingly steep 24,391-bag decline in warehouse certified coffee stocks for the week ended October 18 was attributable to past errors in reporting.
"We do not gather the information ourselves, we report what the warehouses tell us," the spokeswoman said.
The exchange did not say when the removal of the 24,391 bags actually took place, and there are no plans at this time to publish a revised track of stocks.

The CSCE also declined to say which warehouse was responsible for the reporting errors. The exchange's weekly tally includes coffee stocks certified for delivery against the "C" futures contract housed in warehouses in New York, New Orleans, San Francisco and Miami.

Since Monday's report of the stock drawdown, which would have represented a drop of more than 80 percent in exchange inventories, the CSCE spot December futures contract has risen 6.30 cents per lb to close Wednesday at a two-month high of 119.30 cents.
-- Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
